#### Authoring-map sufficiency

The blueprint may be as rich as the required first-pass fidelity demands, but
its richness must be governed and active. The authoring profile may project
only the fields needed by the selected cell while the closure gate evaluates
the complete carrier. At minimum, the authoring map can bind:

- capability promise, identities, version, lineage, and authority digests;
- scenario identities, the declared root, and their semantic partial order;
- each scenario's exact Input, Event, Outcome, contracts, responsibility, and
  terminal disposition;
- declared Outcome variants, predecessor and successor routes, branches, joins,
  and any declared non-monotonic repair or resumption edges;
- applicable semantic altitudes and the operations, transformations,
  mechanics, and provider slots permitted at each altitude;
- governed C4 structural mappings to Context, Container, Component, and
  applicable projected Code identities;
- required capability, product, contract, interface, and precedent bindings;
- artifact ownership and the fixed declarative slots that the selected cell is
  allowed to propose;
- fixtures, invariants, Cross-Apply targets, proof obligations, cell and edge
  observability contracts, and expected evidence addresses;
- SLI definitions, SLO objectives and allocation profiles, applicable SLA
  boundary references, and observability-parity obligations;
- context disclosure, model-role, attempt, effect, cost, and provider-switch
  policies;
- explicit non-claims and forbidden authority expansion; and
- projection profiles, blueprint-review receipt, and the exact blueprint digest
  that every request and receipt must carry.

An admitted blueprint field cannot be decorative. Every declared field must be
consumed by authoring-unit selection, request projection, conformance,
integration, closure, proof, or deterministic revelation. An unsupported field
fails closed; it is not silently ignored. This permits the blueprint schema to
grow without allowing the visible blueprint and the effective authoring map to
diverge.

The bounded request for one cell must contain the cell's exact geometry, valid
predecessor facts, allowed outgoing variants, terminal meaning, applicable
altitude, open declarative slots, vocabulary, dependencies, observability
contract, applicable SLI/SLO/SLA references, proof obligations, non-claims, and
blueprint digest. It must not include unrelated mutable
transcripts, unadmitted sibling testimony, or authority that allows the model
to redesign the capability. “First try” fidelity means the first testimony is
aimed at the exact designed gap; it does not mean testimony bypasses admission
or proof.

#### Capability ownership and migration

The architecture reuses the stronger scenario-scoped circuits rather than
embedding more prompt logic in the package entry point:

| Capability | Required responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `author-capability-candidate-from-feature-reference` | Remains the public feature-reference facade; resolves the feature, obtains one admitted blueprint and digest, and delegates a blueprint-bound request |
| `author-canonical-circuit-blueprint-candidate` | New design circuit that proposes one blueprint candidate from exact feature authority and admitted precedents; its output remains untrusted candidate testimony |
| `inspect-canonical-circuit-blueprint-candidate` | New deterministic circuit that rejects missing geometry, ambiguous semantic precedence, undeclared routes, unsupported structural, observability, or service-level fields, authority drift, and incomplete proof topology before review |
| `project-canonical-circuit-blueprint` | Projects human ASCII, Mermaid, C4, Observability, and Service-Level views plus machine authoring-cell views from the same normalized carrier and returns replay receipts |
| `bind-canonical-blueprint-review` | Binds human approve / hold / reject testimony to exact candidate, carrier, profile, and projection digests |
| `admit-canonical-circuit-blueprint` | New admission circuit that requires conformance and approved review receipts and emits the immutable authoring blueprint authority |
| `author-tooling-capability-candidate` | Becomes the authoring facade/orchestrator; it must stop owning one whole-envelope model request and delegate fabrication to the scenario conveyor |
| `author-capability-scenario-conveyor` | Becomes the blueprint-bound fabrication circuit; its ledger, selection, request, inspection, integration, resumption, and closure all require the same blueprint digest |
| `author-one-scenario-candidate` | Proposes scenario-altitude meaning for only the selected blueprint cell; it cannot choose scenario inventory, semantic precedence, routes, or connectors |
| `author-one-scenario-solution` | Proposes operation and solution-altitude meaning within the selected admitted scenario cell; it cannot select provider realization or rewrite scenario meaning |

The migration is not closed when the target diagram exists, when a prompt
mentions a blueprint, or when the scenario conveyor passes isolated tests. It
is closed only when the `capability:author` live entry point declares and
invokes the blueprint-design and scenario-fabrication dependencies, every model
request and fragment receipt is blueprint-digest-bound, the whole-envelope
authoring route is no longer live, and projected end-to-end proof demonstrates
exact blueprint closure for branching and non-admissible fixtures.

### Provider impact and replaceability

The data center must trace a provider or mechanic through the backplane to every
affected capability, contract, target, and proof obligation. Provider
replacement is admitted only when compatibility, required mechanics,
Cross-Apply equivalence, and live outcome proof close for the affected circuits.
Preserving uptime is insufficient; the replacement must preserve governed
meaning.

### Observability Cross-Apply

Cross-Apply targets may use different telemetry libraries, exporters, and
physical observability providers. They must preserve the canonical blueprint's
semantic measurement identities, attribution checkpoints, correlation and
causal rules, SLI meaning, SLO authority, authorized dimensions, and evidence
lineage.

```text
same semantic address
same SLI identity and calculation
same required testimony checkpoints
same correlation and lineage rules
same SLO authority

different telemetry realization
  allowed only after parity proof
```

An implementation that executes the capability but cannot emit complete,
attributable testimony for every required SLI is not Cross-Apply equivalent.
Provider success, exporter delivery, and telemetry volume alone do not prove
observability parity.

### Reconstruction and recovery

The durable recovery object is the capsule estate plus its canonical
relationships, structural mappings, observability and service-level authority,
environment authority, admission-proof snapshots, and immutable evidence-estate
references. A new environment can restore the registry, resolve eligible
providers and telemetry realizations, project embodiments, reconnect the
semantic backplane, prove circuit and observability closure, and resume operation
without treating historical build output or telemetry as authority.

```text
CAPSULE ESTATE + SEMANTIC BACKPLANE AUTHORITY
  -> RESTORE REGISTRY
  -> RESOLVE PROVIDERS AND TELEMETRY REALIZATIONS
  -> PROJECT EMBODIMENTS
  -> PROVE CIRCUIT AND OBSERVABILITY CLOSURE
  -> RESUME
```

### Governed architectural intelligence

Because the estate's architecture is explicit, SideFX may continuously project
questions such as which circuits are fragile, which capabilities have only one
provider, which products are duplicated, which mechanics fail most often,
which capsules need renewed Cross-Apply proof, and which dependencies approach
deprecation. These analyses nominate governed work. They do not autonomously
change capability meaning, authorize a candidate, or bypass the conveyor.

## Consequences

### Architectural viscosity

Moving from casual file editing to governed mutation introduces intentional
architectural viscosity. Implementation remains easy to regenerate but hard to
treat as authority. A mutation must reveal the capability, declare its semantic
intent, preserve or deliberately revise its design identity, and prove
blueprint closure before the capability can be re-capsuleized and admitted.

### Authoring fidelity

The decided target authoring conveyor receives a bounded projection of the
canonical blueprint before asking a model for testimony. The map fixes the
micro-scenario being authored, its Input / Event / Outcome identities, its valid
routes, the authority available at that altitude, and its proof obligations.
Model output may propose meaning inside that boundary, but it cannot redefine
the map or admit itself.

The current live `capability:author` route does not yet satisfy that decision.
It supplies full feature authority and a whole-artifact profile to one model
request, while the stronger scenario-scoped conveyor remains disconnected and
not blueprint-bound. Until the migration and end-to-end proof obligations in
this ADR close, blueprint-guided first-pass fidelity is a target architecture,
not a property the live authoring entry point may claim.

A conveyor defect is closed by a scenario written specifically for that defect,
plus deterministic conformance and live projected proof. A broad scenario,
successful generation, compilation, projection, or zero exit code does not
close a missing route in the circuit.

### Self-revelation

An admitted capsule must contain or reference sufficient canonical authority to
project its own blueprint—feature, topology, mechanics, dependencies, and proof
state—without requiring the historical source tree or expanded authoring
workspace. This allows a capsule to show what it is autonomously.

### Observability by design

Every executable cell becomes accountable for how its behavior is known, not
only for what it intends to do. Semantic addresses, required testimony,
measurement definitions, and service objectives are reviewed before physical
telemetry bindings exist. Operators can therefore distinguish provider success
from Outcome admission, locate convergence wait, trace branch distribution, and
evaluate experience closure against explicit service authority.

This increases blueprint and proof obligations. It also prevents incidental
metrics, exporter defaults, and dashboard queries from silently defining what
“healthy” means. Measurement authority remains portable across targets while
observed values remain external evidence.

### Continuous circuit integrity

CI/CD becomes integrated-circuit verification. A build is not green merely
because code ran or compiled. It is green only when the physical realization
closes the exact governed circuit that was designed. The release gate validates
that every declared route, node authority, contract, observability obligation,
semantic measurement, and promised outcome remains conformant to the admitted
blueprint. A release can prove measurement capability and attribution parity;
time-windowed production SLO or SLA compliance remains a separate evidence
evaluation.

### Review economics

Pull requests become semantic verification surfaces. The expected review
payload is capability identity, design intent, blueprint delta, structural and
observability mappings, SLI/SLO/SLA deltas, impact, proof, and replayable
execution testimony. This moves reviewer attention away from
reconstructing intent from generated files and toward deciding whether the
right circuit was designed and whether reality faithfully embodied it.

### Replaceable architecture

Capabilities and providers become replaceable modules because their governed
backplane surfaces remain explicit. Removal, isolation, comparison, and
replacement become impact-aware operations over authority and proof rather than
searches through source-level coupling.

### Operational responsibility

The data-center metaphor does not relax governance. It makes authority and
version boundaries more explicit. The system must retain execution lineage,
protect in-flight executions from authority changes, distinguish candidates
from admitted slots, and fail closed when declared and observed mutations do
not match.

### Visible monotonicity

Because every edge carries a declared topology and applicable progress
disposition, a
circuit that merely churns state becomes visually and mechanically suspicious
rather than merely undocumented. A reviewer can see that a transition narrows,
establishes, descends, or terminates, and the monotonic view states the same
fact as a counted disposition. Semantic advancement stops being a claim in prose
and becomes a projected property of the graph.

### One graph, many lenses

Adding a view is adding a governed projection profile, not adding a diagram to
maintain. The estate therefore avoids a second architecture-picture system that
drifts from authority, and any tooling that renders a view — including Mermaid
itself — can be replaced without touching blueprint meaning.

## The five foundational blueprint laws

### 1. Canonical Blueprint Law

> Every admitted capability SHALL possess one canonical, machine-readable
> circuit blueprint describing its governed semantic topology, structural
> mappings, observability contracts, and service-level design across applicable
> altitudes.

### 2. Blueprint Projection Law

> Human diagrams, execution maps, dependency views, impact views, and
> implementation views SHALL be projections of canonical blueprint authority
> and SHALL NOT become competing sources of truth.

### 3. Blueprint Closure Law

> A capability SHALL NOT be admitted or re-capsuleized after mutation unless
> its realized authority, required routes, contracts, mechanics, dependencies,
> observability contracts, service-level authority, and proof obligations
> conform to its canonical blueprint.

### 4. Self-Revelation Law

> An admitted capsule SHALL contain or reference sufficient canonical authority
> to project its own blueprint, structural mappings, observability design, and
> service-level authority without requiring its expanded workspace.

### 5. Authority Precedence and No-Duplicate Authority Law

> Feature authority SHALL own promise, scenario intent, human semantic
> expression, and root Input / Event / Outcome meaning; blueprint authority
> SHALL own designed topology, structural mappings, observability contracts,
> SLI/SLO definitions and allocations, and fabrication boundaries; separately
> governed SLA authority SHALL own external service commitments; capability
> authority SHALL own the completed declarative realization. Downstream
> authority SHALL reference rather than re-author an upstream-owned fact. Any
> necessary repeated representation SHALL be digest-bound and mechanically
> proven identical.

## Capability data-center and authoring laws

### 6. Semantic Backplane Law

> Capability circuits SHALL connect through governed semantic identities,
> products, contracts, routes, dependencies, interfaces, observability and
> service-level identities, and evidence obligations. A consumer SHALL NOT
> require another capability's source layout
> or private implementation as integration authority. An Outcome SHALL state
> what became true, SHALL establish a product or observable state where
> downstream composition is required, and that product SHALL satisfy the
> consumer's admitted Input; Outcome and product SHALL NOT be treated as
> interchangeable authority.

### 7. Quarantine Mutation Law

> Mutation of an admitted capability SHALL occur as an isolated candidate in a
> governed quarantine boundary. The currently admitted capsule SHALL remain
> authoritative until a replacement candidate independently proves closure and
> is admitted.

### 8. Version-Pinned Execution Law

> Every execution SHALL be attributable to the exact capability identity,
> authority digest, capsule digest, and admitted version that governed its
> start, with correlation and causal lineage through every required cell and
> provider realization. Replacement admission SHALL NOT alter the authority of
> an in-flight execution.

### 9. Semantic Delta Law

> Review and admission SHALL compare the declared blueprint mutation with the
> observed authority, circuit, dependency, interface, structural mapping,
> observability, service-level, projection, and proof mutation. Any unexplained
> difference SHALL be rejected as an undeclared architectural mutation.

### 10. Evidence Replay Law

> Test and production testimony SHALL remain addressable against the same
> canonical blueprint identities used at design time and SHALL remain in the
> execution evidence estate rather than mutate the design-identity capsule.
> A capsule MAY embed a frozen admission-proof snapshot and immutable evidence
> references. Observed SLI values, SLO compliance, error-budget state, and SLA
> breach testimony SHALL follow the same rule. Replay MAY explain where
> execution diverged; testimony SHALL NOT redefine authority or self-admit an
> undeclared route.

### 11. Semantic Reconstruction Law

> The admitted capsule estate, its canonical semantic backplane authority, and
> required environment bindings SHALL be sufficient to reconstruct and re-prove
> supported physical embodiments without historical build output becoming
> authority.

### 12. Governed Evolution Law

> Estate observation and analysis MAY nominate fragile circuits, provider
> concentration, duplicated products, proof staleness, or dependency risk.
> Such findings SHALL enter governed authoring and admission; they SHALL NOT
> autonomously mutate capability meaning.

### 13. Deterministic Blueprint Projection Law

> ASCII, Mermaid, C4, Observability, Service-Level, and every other human
> blueprint view SHALL be deterministic
> projections of one canonical circuit-blueprint carrier. Identical
> lineage-bound blueprint authority, projector authority, and
> projection-profile authority SHALL
> reproduce byte-identical projection source and digests. A projected view
> SHALL NOT invent, omit, or reinterpret semantic precedence, scenario geometry,
> branches, terminal dispositions, mechanics, or provider slots. Projection
> ordinals MAY deterministically order independent peers for display but SHALL
> NOT create semantic or execution precedence.

### 14. Human Blueprint Review Law

> Capability authority SHALL NOT become eligible for collapse and admission
> after authoring or mutation until a designated human has received the
> deterministic blueprint projections and every required structural,
> observability, and service-level review view, and an approve disposition has been
> bound to their exact authority, carrier, profile, and output digests. Any
> governed blueprint or projection-profile mutation SHALL invalidate the review
> receipt and require re-projection and re-review. Designated human approval is
> a permanent and universal obligation under this ADR, not a replaceable
> assurance profile.

### 15. Blueprint-Guided Authoring Law

> Every model request in capability fabrication SHALL be a deterministic,
> digest-bound projection of exactly one eligible canonical-blueprint cell.
> Model testimony SHALL NOT select or redefine scenario inventory, semantic
> precedence, cell geometry, variants, routes, altitude, dependencies,
> artifact ownership, structural mappings, mechanics, provider slots,
> observability contracts, SLI/SLO/SLA authority, or proof obligations.

### 16. Active Blueprint Authority Law

> Every field admitted into a canonical blueprint SHALL govern at least one
> authoring-unit selection, request projection, conformance, integration,
> closure, proof, impact, or revelation decision. A declared blueprint field
> that the active circuit cannot consume SHALL fail closed and SHALL NOT be
> ignored as decorative or prompt-only context.

### 17. Blueprint-Bound Authoring Closure Law

> A capability candidate SHALL NOT be assembled or handed off as closed until
> every required blueprint cell, route, contract, dependency, artifact slot,
> mechanic, provider slot, observability contract, SLI/SLO authority,
> applicable SLA boundary, fixture, and proof obligation is closed against the
> reviewed canonical-blueprint digest. Scenario-ledger completeness or artifact
> cardinality alone SHALL NOT establish blueprint closure.

## Canonical blueprint geometry laws

### 18. Canonical Blueprint Geometry Law

> Every capability blueprint SHALL represent its governed scenario circuit as
> typed semantic states, responsibilities, outcomes, junctions, and
> relationships. Branching, fan-out, convergence, altitude descent,
> termination, and monotonic advancement SHALL be explicit graph semantics
> rather than inferred from implementation control flow. ASCII, Mermaid, and
> interactive SideFX diagrams SHALL be deterministic projections of the same
> canonical blueprint graph. Scenario, execution, mechanic, and provider cells
> SHALL preserve the three-position cell protocol while using the semantic nouns
> proper to their altitude; lower physical results SHALL NOT be relabeled as
> promised experiences.

### 19. Orthogonal Edge Semantics Law

> Every blueprint edge SHALL carry exactly one topological role and the contract
> relation, semantic-progress disposition, and selecting Outcome variant
> applicable to that role. A branch route and any variant-selected bounded
> return SHALL name the exact selecting variant; every executable transition
> SHALL declare progress; a contract edge SHALL declare `SATISFIES` or
> `REQUIRES`. A projector SHALL NOT collapse these dimensions, infer any field
> from adjacency or projection ordinal, or present alternative routes into a
> shared node as convergence.

### 20. Monotonic Advancement Law

> Every executable forward transition SHALL narrow admitted state, establish a
> new required product, descend to a lower altitude, or terminate an obligation.
> A transition that widens or churns admitted state without a declared semantic-
> progress disposition SHALL fail closed. Where canonical authority declares a
> bounded repair, resumption, or iteration edge, the projection SHALL show that
> `BOUNDED_RETURN` edge and its bound rather than presenting the circuit as
> monotonic.

### 21. Blueprint View Law

> Scenario, monotonic, branch, dependency, altitude, C4, provider,
> Observability, Service-Level, evidence, runtime, and semantic-diff views SHALL
> be governed lenses over one canonical
> blueprint graph sharing its nodes, edges, identities, and digests. A view
> SHALL NOT introduce a second diagram authoring system, a hand-maintained
> picture, or a node or edge that the canonical graph does not declare.
> Evidence and Runtime / Play views MAY overlay separately digested testimony
> bound to canonical identities; such overlays SHALL NOT become blueprint nodes
> or edges or alter the blueprint digest.

## Observability and service-level laws

### 22. Observability-by-Design Law

> Every executable blueprint cell SHALL declare sufficient observability
> authority to attribute its input admission, responsibility invocation,
> provider realization, result or Outcome admission, and relevant evidence to
> the exact semantic address, causal identity, execution identity, and authority
> digest that governed it. Observability SHALL be designed before realization
> rather than inferred afterward from implementation telemetry.

### 23. Semantic SLI Law

> Every declared SLI SHALL define the exact admitted testimony from which it is
> calculated, its semantic scope, authorized dimensions, aggregation rule,
> evaluation window, freshness rule, missing-testimony disposition, and unit.
> An implementation metric SHALL NOT become an SLI merely because it is
> available to observe.

### 24. SLO Authority Law

> Every SLO SHALL bind one or more admitted SLI definitions to explicit target
> conditions, evaluation windows, and error-budget policy. SLO decomposition or
> budget allocation across child circuit cells SHALL be explicitly governed and
> SHALL NOT be inferred from topology, measured latency, or provider behavior.

### 25. SLA Boundary Law

> An SLA SHALL bind externally governed service obligations to admitted SLO
> authority at a declared capability, product, interface, platform, provider, or
> customer-facing experience boundary. Internal mechanics MAY contribute SLI or
> SLO evidence but SHALL NOT acquire contractual SLA semantics unless explicit
> SLA authority binds that service boundary.

### 26. Observability Cross-Apply Law

> Cross-Apply targets MAY use different physical observability providers,
> telemetry libraries, and exporters, but SHALL preserve equivalent semantic
> measurement identities, attribution checkpoints, correlation rules, SLI
> meaning, SLO authority, authorized dimensions, and evidence lineage for every
> observability obligation required by the canonical blueprint.

## The single bootstrap law

### 27. Single Bootstrap Law

> SideFX SHALL have exactly one bootstrap boundary: the minimum physical
> capability required to operate capsules. Every other behavior, including
> authoring, projection, verification, change management, observability,
> service-level evaluation, and platform evolution, SHALL exist as governed
> capability authority and SHALL use the ordinary capability lifecycle.

One bootstrap. Everything else is capability.

A discovered gap is never permission to leave the capability model. When a
required outcome cannot be established, the correct statement is not "we need a
bootstrap for this" but "an existing capability does not yet fulfil this
outcome" or "this capability does not yet exist". Both statements resolve the
same way:

```text
DO WE HAVE THE CAPABILITY?
        |
      +---+
      |   |
     YES  NO
      |   |
      |   v
      |  AUTHOR THE CAPABILITY
      |  THROUGH THE NORMAL
      |  GOVERNED PATH
      |
      v
FULFILL THE OUTCOME
```

Either the capability exists, or capability work exists.

Without this law, every newly discovered need becomes a candidate exception, and
the estate accretes a privileged path beside the governed one for each gap it
ever met. That is the semantic fragmentation the capsule model exists to
eliminate, reintroduced under an approving name. A second bootstrap is not a
smaller architecture; it is a second architecture.

## Architectural self-description

Given only an admitted capsule, the revelation circuit must be able to answer:

> **Show me what you are.**

The answer can deterministically project the capability's:

- feature;
- canonical blueprint;
- scenario topology;
- typed nodes and orthogonal edge topology, contract, progress, and variant
  semantics;
- C4 Context, Container, Component, and applicable projected Code mappings;
- branch junctions, fan-out sets, and convergence requirement sets;
- monotonic disposition and its counted summary;
- Inputs, Events, and Outcomes;
- cell and edge observability contracts;
- semantic addresses, testimony requirements, correlation rules, measurements,
  dimensions, sampling, and evidence destinations;
- SLI definitions, SLO objectives, allocation profiles, and error-budget
  policies;
- applicable SLA identities, service boundaries, and obligation references;
- admitted version and authority identity;
- dependencies;
- mechanics;
- provider slots;
- proof state;
- Cross-Apply state;
- projection targets and declared views;
- frozen admission-proof snapshot and immutable references to attributable
  execution evidence; and
- admitted effect and experience closure.

The revelation circuit resolves referenced runtime testimony from the execution
evidence estate. New test or production executions do not change the capsule
digest; they become newly attributable evidence under the capsule's immutable
identities. Observed SLI values, SLO compliance, remaining error budgets, SLA
breach dispositions, and execution history are resolved as evidence overlays;
they are not rewritten into the design capsule.

When supplied another capsule and the applicable estate/backplane authority,
deterministic review projections can additionally reveal semantic and blueprint
deltas plus affected routes, contracts, capabilities, interfaces, providers,
and targets. Those comparisons do not require either capsule's historical
source workspace.

The capsule describes itself. It does not authorize itself: digest, schema,
authority closure, execution-plan integrity, blueprint closure, and proof
obligations remain admission decisions.

## Product model

```text
CAPABILITY
  =
PROMISE
  +
CIRCUIT
  +
STRUCTURE
  +
OBSERVABILITY
  +
SERVICE LEVELS
  +
AUTHORITY
  +
PROOF
  +
PORTABILITY
```

The capsule is its package. The blueprint is its semantic, flow, structural,
observability, and service-level design. The conveyor is its fabrication
process. Cross-Apply is adversarial verification. Projection is physical
realization. Execution energizes the circuit. Evidence is the return signal.
CI/CD is continuous circuit integrity.

The resulting product is not a source-code component or merely “AI-generated
software.” It is a sealed, inspectable, executable integrated circuit of
meaning around which the SideFX environment can organize.

At estate altitude:

```text
CAPABILITY DATA CENTER
  =
CAPSULE ESTATE
  +
CANONICAL BLUEPRINTS
  +
SEMANTIC BACKPLANE
  +
STRUCTURAL MAPPINGS
  +
OBSERVABILITY AND SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHORITY
  +
QUARANTINE AND ADMISSION
  +
PROJECTION AND EXECUTION
  +
EXECUTION EVIDENCE ESTATE
```

The operating vocabulary is therefore intentional: **insert, remove, isolate,
reveal, materialize, modify, prove, collapse, admit, replace, replay, and
restore**. Each verb must resolve to a governed capability circuit or a
deterministic projection of one; none authorizes hand-editing physical output.

## Implementation obligations

This ADR establishes accepted architectural direction; acceptance does not
claim that every control-room projection or operating capability is already
admitted. Delivery must proceed through canonical features and micro-scenarios
for at least these bounded responsibilities:

1. **Author a canonical blueprint candidate:** derive one lineage-bound circuit
   design from exact canonical feature authority and admitted precedents without
   allowing model testimony to self-admit, overwrite explicit feature facts, or
   create duplicate ownership of an upstream fact.
2. **Inspect canonical blueprint conformance:** reject ambiguous or missing
   semantic precedence, missing altitude-appropriate cell geometry, untyped
   nodes or edges, collapsed or incomplete edge semantics, undeclared routes,
   unsupported fields, incomplete terminals, incomplete convergence requirement
   sets, unexplained state widening, undeclared back edges, authority drift,
   duplicate authority, missing observability coverage, invalid SLI/SLO/SLA
   bindings, and incomplete proof topology before review.
3. **Resolve canonical circuit authority:** construct one deterministic
   `canonical-circuit-blueprint.v1` carrier from a conformant lineage-bound
   candidate or admitted scenario, transition, mechanic, provider-slot,
   terminal, and digest authority, preserving semantic partial order separately
   from projection ordinals without upgrading a candidate's disposition.
4. **Project deterministic blueprint views:** produce byte-stable ASCII and
   Mermaid source plus replay receipts from one carrier through versioned
   projection profiles, carry the declared node kind and orthogonal edge
   semantics on every projected element, use projection ordinals only for
   deterministic display, project each declared blueprint view — including C4,
   Observability, and Service-Level views — from the same carrier, and project
   machine authoring cells from the same digest-bound carrier.
5. **Bind human blueprint review:** present the deterministic projections and
   bind approve / hold / reject testimony to their exact authority and output
   digests.
6. **Admit the authoring blueprint:** require deterministic conformance and one
   current approved blueprint-review receipt before emitting immutable
   blueprint authority eligible to guide fabrication.
7. **Bind the public authoring facade:** revise
   `author-capability-candidate-from-feature-reference` so the live
   `capability:author` entry point resolves and passes the admitted blueprint
   carrier and digest instead of delegating feature authority alone.
8. **Operate blueprint-bound scenario fabrication:** revise
   `author-tooling-capability-candidate` to delegate to
   `author-capability-scenario-conveyor`, and require every ledger, cell
   selection, model request, fragment receipt, integration, resumption, and
   closure decision to carry the same blueprint digest.
9. **Author one altitude-bounded cell:** use the one-scenario candidate and
   solution circuits only for the exact scenario and altitude selected by the
   blueprint, with no model-selected topology, connectors, routes, artifacts,
   structural mappings, mechanics, providers, observability contracts,
   SLI/SLO/SLA authority, or proof obligations.
10. **Prove the live authoring migration:** demonstrate through the package
    `capability:author` entry point that branching and non-admissible fixtures
    receive cell-scoped requests, close every blueprint obligation, and cannot
    reach the retired whole-envelope model route.
11. **Reveal capability design identity:** compose the canonical blueprint,
   projection receipts, review state, frozen admission-proof snapshot, external
   evidence references, and self-description from one admitted capsule without
   reconstructing topology from a scenario-name list or embedding open-ended
   runtime testimony.
12. **Compare capability designs:** produce a deterministic semantic, blueprint,
   structural, observability, service-level, dependency, interface, and proof
   delta between two capsules.
13. **Trace mutation impact:** identify affected scenarios, contracts,
   capabilities, structural mappings, SLIs, SLOs, SLAs, providers, interfaces,
   and Cross-Apply targets.
14. **Verify declared mutation:** reject any observed change not closed by the
   declared blueprint delta.
15. **Play an admitted circuit:** execute a canonical fixture, bind ordered
   testimony to blueprint node and edge identities, and expose convergence
   readiness, SLI observations, SLO budget consumption, and applicable SLA
   disposition without making the visualization authoritative.
16. **Replay execution evidence:** compare design-time, test, and production
   testimony and service-level evaluation through stable semantic addresses.
17. **Operate a quarantine lifecycle:** isolate an admitted version, reveal and
    materialize it, author a candidate replacement, prove it, and either admit
    or reject it without disturbing the admitted slot.
18. **Switch admitted versions safely:** pin in-flight executions and advance a
    capability slot only through an atomic, evidence-backed admission decision.
19. **Assess provider replacement:** trace provider impact and prove semantic
    and observability equivalence before rebinding affected circuits.
20. **Project the capability control room:** show estate health, candidates,
    quarantines, dependencies, proof freshness, blueprint-review state, and
    execution, observability, SLO, error-budget, and SLA state as deterministic
    views.
21. **Reconstruct the capability data center:** restore the capsule registry,
    resolve environment authority and telemetry-realization bindings, project
    embodiments, reconnect the backplane and evidence destinations, and re-prove
    circuit and observability closure from a clean environment.
22. **Nominate architectural improvement:** analyze estate evidence and produce
    bounded findings that enter the ordinary authoring conveyor without
    self-authorizing change.
23. **Prove blueprint geometry conformance:** verify that every node carries a
    declared kind, every edge carries exactly one topological role and all
    applicable contract, progress, and variant fields, every branch route and
    variant-selected bounded return names an exact declared Outcome variant,
    every fan-out set is jointly required, every convergence node declares its
    complete required-product set, and every route reaches a declared terminal.
24. **Project the monotonic view:** emit the deterministic advancement-only
    projection and its counted summary — semantic states, executable forward
    transitions, edges by topology, progress dispositions, contract relations,
    declared branch and fan-out sets, convergence sets, terminal paths,
    undeclared back edges, unexplained widening, and ambiguous
    transitions — with a `CONFORMS` or exact holding disposition.
25. **Author observability contracts:** bind every executable cell and applicable
    edge to required testimony checkpoints, semantic and causal addresses,
    measurements, authorized dimensions, sampling, evidence destinations, and
    exact authority digests before physical telemetry realization.
26. **Resolve semantic SLIs:** construct admitted SLI definitions only from exact
    admitted testimony identities, scopes, calculation rules, windows,
    freshness, units, and incomplete-evidence dispositions; reject incidental
    implementation metrics as undeclared indicators.
27. **Bind SLO authority and allocations:** bind admitted SLIs to explicit
    targets, evaluation windows, error-budget policies, and any governed child-
    cell allocation profiles without inferring a root objective from topology or
    observations.
28. **Bind applicable SLA boundaries:** reference external service obligations
    only at declared capability, product, interface, platform, provider, or
    customer-facing experience boundaries and reject contractual leakage into
    unbound internal mechanics.
29. **Prove observability Cross-Apply:** demonstrate that every target preserves
    semantic measurement identity, attribution checkpoints, correlation rules,
    SLI meaning, SLO authority, authorized dimensions, and evidence lineage even
    when telemetry libraries, exporters, and providers differ.
30. **Evaluate and project service levels:** evaluate admitted SLI/SLO/SLA
    authority over an exact bounded evidence set; emit C4, Observability,
    Service-Level, and Play overlays with authority and evidence digests; and
    never treat a partial evaluation window as a satisfied production promise.

Each responsibility requires exact altitude-appropriate cell geometry, authority
lineage, deterministic conformance, observability closure, and live outcome
proof. A scenario cell uses Input / Event / Outcome; lower cells retain the
three-position protocol with their own semantic nouns. A dashboard, diagram,
model response, workspace, telemetry stream, exporter delivery, or successful
projection alone does not satisfy any obligation above.

## Product statement

> **SideFX turns software architecture into an operable capability data center:
> sealed semantic circuits can be revealed, isolated, structurally mapped,
> observed, evaluated against governed service levels, redesigned, proven,
> replaced, replayed, and restored without making implementation or telemetry
> the source of truth.**
