# ADR-001: Design-Identity Capability Capsules and the Capability Data Center

**Status:** Accepted

**Date:** 2026-08-21

**Amended:** 2026-08-22

## Context

SideFX has crossed a product boundary. A capsule already provides a durable,
portable unit of capability, but durability alone does not give that unit a
unique, inspectable design identity. Treating generated files, workspaces, or
human-drawn diagrams as the design leaves semantic authority fragmented and
allows implementation artifacts to compete with meaning.

The architecture therefore moves from conventional software editing toward the
engineering of executable promises. The capability capsule remains the durable
unit. A canonical circuit blueprint gives that unit its specific design
identity.

At estate altitude, SideFX also needs an operating model for how those durable
units are connected, inspected, changed, replaced, replayed, and restored.
Conventional source review makes a reviewer reconstruct intent from physical
implementation. That is architectural archaeology. A design-identity capsule
can invert the review object: reveal the intended circuit, show its exact
semantic mutation, trace its impact, and present the evidence that does or does
not justify admission.

## Decision

SideFX will adopt the **Capability Capsule** and **Canonical Blueprint** model.
The canonical blueprint is the machine-readable structured graph authority for
a capability across every applicable semantic altitude. Visual diagrams,
execution maps, dependency views, impact views, and implementation views are
strictly deterministic projections of that authority.

The execution model has fractal cell geometry. Every altitude preserves one
three-position cell protocol, but each altitude uses the semantic nouns proper
to it. Authority expands outward from scenario meaning through execution,
mechanics, and governed provider references. Evidence contracts back through
that same circuit toward the promised outcome.

```text
PROMISE
  -> SCENARIO CELL  [Input -> Event -> Outcome]
    -> EXECUTION CELL [Input -> Responsibility -> Result]
      -> MECHANIC CELL [Input -> Mechanic -> Result]
        -> PROVIDER CELL [Physical Input -> Native Operation -> Physical Result]

EVIDENCE
  <- provider testimony
  <- mechanic result
  <- operation result
  <- scenario outcome
  <- promised experience
```

The blueprint is authority; the diagram above is only a projection explaining
that authority.

That authority is a **typed semantic graph**, not a flowchart. Its nodes carry
declared kinds — state, responsibility, outcome, junction, convergence, provider
slot, terminal — and its edges carry orthogonal topology, contract, semantic-
progress, and selecting-variant fields. Branching, fan-out, convergence,
altitude descent, termination, and monotonic advancement are explicit graph
semantics. They are never inferred from implementation control flow, node
adjacency, or the order in which a projector happened to walk the graph.

At estate altitude, SideFX will operate these sealed circuits as a **Capability
Data Center**. Capabilities connect through a governed semantic backplane rather
than arbitrary knowledge of one another's implementations. The data center is
an architectural operating model, not a filesystem layout or deployment
topology.

| Architectural concept | SideFX meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Integrated circuit | One capability's governed promise, circuit, authority, proof, and portability |
| Capsule | Sealed, content-addressed package for that circuit |
| Canonical blueprint | Machine-readable design identity and graph authority |
| Capability data center | The operable estate of admitted and candidate capability circuits |
| Semantic backplane | Governed identities, contracts, products, routes, dependencies, interfaces, observability and service-level identities, and evidence obligations connecting circuits |
| Logical rack | A projected grouping such as product, domain, platform, team, or environment; never authority by physical placement |
| Quarantine bay | An isolated candidate-mutation boundary in which an admitted capsule may be revealed, materialized, changed, and re-proven |
| Control room | Deterministic projections for estate health, inspection, impact, execution, observability, service-level evaluation, and evidence replay |
| Play | Execution of an admitted circuit with semantic addresses, actual testimony, and applicable service-level budget illuminated |
| Observability contract | Blueprint authority declaring how execution and outcomes become attributable evidence |
| SLI | Governed measurement definition over exact admitted testimony |
| SLO | Governed target and evaluation window over one or more admitted SLIs |
| SLA | External service obligation bound to admitted SLO authority at a declared service boundary |
| Continuous circuit integrity | Admission and release verification that physical realization still closes the designed circuit |

### Complete capability design identity

The design identity spans semantic intent, circuit flow, structural realization,
service expectations, and evidence design:

```text
CAPABILITY DESIGN IDENTITY

PROMISE             feature and promised experience
SEMANTIC DESIGN     canonical blueprint
FLOW DESIGN         monotonic circuit and governed bounded returns
STRUCTURAL DESIGN   C4 Context / Container / Component / Code projections
SERVICE DESIGN      SLI / SLO authority and applicable SLA bindings
EVIDENCE DESIGN     observability contracts and testimony lineage
REALIZATION         providers, targets, and embodiments
EXECUTION           actual circuit traversal
PROOF               conformance, Cross-Apply, and closure
```

C4 views are governed structural lenses over blueprint, execution-plan, and
physical-realization authority. The C4 Code lens, when applicable, reveals
projected embodiment structure; it never turns generated code into authored
design authority or relaxes the repository's projection-only implementation
law.

## Capability data-center operating model

### Semantic backplane

A capability does not depend on another capability's source layout or internal
implementation. It connects through governed semantic surfaces:

```text
Capability A
  -> Outcome A
  -> ESTABLISHES Product A / Observable State
  -> SATISFIES admitted Input B
  -> Capability B
```

The semantic backplane consists of capability identities, Inputs, Events,
Outcomes, products, scenario transitions, required capabilities, provider
requirements, interface contracts, compatibility profiles, observability
contracts, SLI/SLO identities, applicable SLA boundary references, and evidence
obligations. These surfaces make a circuit replaceable because consumers own
their contract with the backplane, not the producer's internals. Outcomes state
what becomes true; products or observable states state what becomes available
to satisfy downstream Inputs. They are related but never interchangeable.

### Three operating planes

The data center separates three planes without disconnecting them:

| Plane | Governing question | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability plane | What can the enterprise do, why must it become true, and what service is promised? | Promise, feature, scenarios, responsibilities, outcomes, service boundaries, applicable SLA references, and admitted capsule identity |
| Circuit plane | How do capabilities and their products compose, and how is good behavior defined? | Routes, transitions, contracts, dependencies, mechanics, observability contracts, semantic SLIs, SLOs, allocation profiles, provider slots, and proof obligations |
| Physical plane | Where, through what, and with which telemetry realization does a responsibility execute? | Target profiles, projected embodiments, runtimes, operating systems, infrastructure, model or human providers, effect bindings, telemetry libraries, and exporter bindings |

Authority expands from the capability plane toward physical realization.
Evidence returns from the physical plane through the same semantic addresses.
No physical realization is permitted to redefine the capability or circuit
planes.

### Authority precedence and ownership

Canonical ownership flows in one direction:

```text
FEATURE AUTHORITY
  owns promise, scenario intent, human semantic expression,
  and root Input / Event / Outcome meaning
        |
        v constrains
BLUEPRINT AUTHORITY
  owns designed topology, routes, variants, joins, altitude map,
  structural mappings, observability contracts, SLI/SLO definitions,
  SLO allocation profiles, authoring boundaries, and proof topology
        |
        v constrains
CAPABILITY AUTHORITY
  owns the completed declarative realization of the admitted design
        |
        v projects
EXECUTION PLAN
  owns the physical realization plan
        |
        v sealed in or referenced from
CAPSULE
  packages the durable design identity
```

Downstream authority references upstream facts; it does not independently
re-author them. Where a projection or carrier repeats an upstream fact for
portability or deterministic inspection, the repetition is digest-bound and
mechanically proven identical to its canonical owner. A repeated representation
that can drift is duplicate authority and must fail closed.

SLA authority is separately governed at a declared capability, product,
interface, platform, provider, or customer-facing service boundary. It binds
parties and external obligations to admitted SLO identities without becoming
blueprint-owned business contract text or leaking contractual semantics into
internal mechanic cells.

### Governed quarantine and replacement

An admitted capability is never edited in place. Mutation creates an isolated
candidate replacement:

```text
ADMITTED SLOT: capability X / authority v17
  -> EJECT FROM AUTHORING POSITION
  -> OPEN GOVERNED QUARANTINE BAY
  -> REVEAL CAPSULE AND CANONICAL BLUEPRINT
  -> MATERIALIZE DISPOSABLE ENGINEERING WORKSPACE
  -> DECLARE AND AUTHOR BOUNDED SEMANTIC MUTATION
  -> CONFORM, REVIEW, REPAIR, AND PROVE BLUEPRINT CLOSURE
  -> COLLAPSE CANDIDATE CAPSULE v18
  -> CROSS-APPLY, EXECUTE, AND PROVE CANDIDATE CAPSULE
  -> ADMIT OR REJECT CANDIDATE
  -> INSERT v18 INTO THE GOVERNED SLOT ONLY AFTER ADMISSION
```

Version 17 remains admitted while version 18 is a candidate. An execution is
pinned to the exact capability identity, authority digest, capsule digest, and
version under which it begins. In-flight execution under version 17 completes
under version 17 authority; admission of version 18 does not rewrite its
meaning. “Hot swap” therefore means versioned, governed replacement at an
explicit execution boundary—not casual mutation during execution.

The quarantine bay is a semantic isolation boundary. A temporary directory may
be one physical realization of it, but the directory is not the quarantine
authority and never becomes durable capability meaning.

### Governed change lifecycle and mainline closure

Every new or replacement capability travels through one governed lifecycle:

The normalized operational expansion—including design review, `AUTHOR`, `PROVE`,
repository transport, and fail-closed stage evidence—is
[Capability change lifecycle](capability-change-lifecycle.md). It is the single
operational sequence; this ADR remains its architectural authority.

```text
REVIEWED FEATURE-AUTHORITY CANDIDATE + APPROVED CANONICAL BLUEPRINT
  -> OPEN      establish exact baseline, impact, and quarantine boundary
  -> AUTHOR    fabricate only blueprint-selected cells inside that boundary
  -> PROVE     deterministically admit, project, test, and close proof
  -> SEAL      authoritatively collapse the capsule and bind its proof lineage
  -> PUBLISH   atomically admit the capsule and advance the repository estate
  -> PUSH      transport the bounded publication set from main to origin/main
  -> OBSERVE   resolve the resulting state from durable mainline authority
```

CLI, API, and MCP are protocol projections over this authority. They may bind
carriers, invoke the lifecycle capabilities, and render governed results; they
do not own lifecycle meaning and may not infer a more favorable state.

`OPEN` fixes the exact admitted baseline, authorized mutation set, impact proof
set, and isolated authoring boundary. Before any blueprint cell can guide
fabrication, deterministic blueprint conformance and the current reviewer
approval must bind the exact reviewer authority digest, review-boundary digest,
canonical-blueprint digest, and feature bytes. No model request, workbench
fragment, or integration decision may select or silently replace those facts.

`SEAL` is eligible only after source admission, projection, fixtures,
Cross-Apply obligations, prospective dependency closure, and all applicable
blueprint obligations pass. It owns authoritative capsule collapse, requires
capsule integrity, reconstruction/round-trip closure, and reproducibility, and
then binds the exact candidate capsule digest, proof receipt, and repository
lineage. A direct scratch pack is rehearsal testimony; it is neither SEAL nor
publication.

`PUBLISH` revalidates the baseline against current mainline and performs the
admitted estate effect atomically. In this repository that effect records the
capsule, advances the capsule-estate manifest and bootstrap eligibility, and
retains the exact feature and blueprint identities carried by the capsule. The
resulting publication set is transported as one bounded commit to `main` and
pushed to `origin/main`; the estate manifest is never hand-edited as a
substitute for the admitted effect.

`OBSERVE` derives status from the durable capsule, feature, estate manifest,
bootstrap authority, and repository relationship. A candidate, workbench,
packed artifact, local estate mutation, commit that has not been pushed, or a
successful command in `C:\lab\delete-me` is not a published capability.

A capability change is complete only when all of these are simultaneously
true:

- the lifecycle publication outcome is `PUBLISHED`, `COMPLETE`, and
  `SUCCEEDED`, with admission recorded and zero findings;
- the exact bounded publication set is committed on local `main` and pushed so
  local `main` equals `origin/main`;
- the durable worktree is clean and contains no unintegrated capability
  surface from that change;
- the capsule estate and bootstrap counts agree and estate verification is
  `verified` with zero findings;
- required repository tests pass; and
- observation resolves the exact admitted capability as `PUBLISHED` from
  durable mainline authority.

Promotion is incremental. Once one independently reviewed capability change is
eligible, it advances immediately; it does not wait in a disposable workspace
for unrelated candidates or a large integration batch. An explicitly approved
atomic review boundary may group inseparable changes, but batch convenience
alone is not atomicity.

Repository-mainline publication and remote content-addressed object-store
publication are separate planes. The former is admitted here. The latter
remains governed by the remote durable-storage acceptance plan and cannot be
inferred from a successful Git push.

### Semantic review instead of source archaeology

The primary review object is a self-explaining capsule and its semantic delta,
not a source-code diff. The capsule becomes a self-explaining change set. A
review projection must answer:

```text
WHO I AM       capability identity and authority digest
WHY I EXIST    feature intent and promised experience
WHAT I DO      scenario circuit and Input / Event / Outcome geometry
HOW I DO IT    execution authority, mechanics, and provider slots
HOW I AM BUILT governed C4 structural mappings and projected embodiments
HOW I AM KNOWN observability contracts, testimony, correlation, and evidence lineage
WHAT GOOD MEANS
                SLI definitions, SLO targets, allocation profiles, and applicable SLA bindings
WHAT CHANGED   semantic and blueprint delta
WHAT I AFFECT  routes, contracts, dependencies, interfaces, and targets
HOW I WAS PROVEN
                fixtures, conformance, blueprint closure, and Cross-Apply
WHAT HAPPENED  execution testimony and replayable observations
WHAT RESULTED  admitted outcome and experience closure
```

Review compares the declared mutation with the observed authority mutation,
including structural, observability, and service-level authority:

```text
DECLARED BLUEPRINT DELTA
          <->
OBSERVED AUTHORITY / CIRCUIT DELTA
```

Any unexplained difference is an
`UNDECLARED_ARCHITECTURAL_MUTATION` and must be rejected. A reviewer should
reason about intended experience, scenario correctness, dependency
justification, blueprint coverage, and evidence sufficiency. Projector output
formatting and implementation trivia belong to deterministic projection and
conformance unless they expose a semantic or realization defect.

SideFX separates two review moments:

1. **Design review:** Does intent, feature, blueprint, scenario topology, and
   responsibility geometry describe the right circuit?
2. **Realization review:** Did projection, execution, providers, and observed
   evidence faithfully embody that admitted circuit?

### Executable inspection and evidence replay

“Play” is a deterministic execution view over an admitted blueprint and actual
execution testimony. It is not an animation authored separately from the
circuit. The execution plan already carries semantic addresses, altitude,
Input contracts, execution-authority identities and digests, provider slots,
Outcome contracts, source pointers, and source-authority digests. A Play
projection binds ordered testimony to those addresses and illuminates the route
that actually executed.

Design-time expectation, test execution, and production execution must remain
comparable through the same identities:

```text
DESIGN-TIME BLUEPRINT
          <->
TEST EXECUTION TESTIMONY
          <->
PRODUCTION EXECUTION TESTIMONY
```

Telemetry is replayable evidence, not a separate source of meaning. It may show
where a provider timed out, a retry occurred, an Outcome was rejected, or an
experience failed to close. It cannot alter the blueprint, select admission,
or claim that an undeclared route was valid.

Open-ended runtime testimony remains outside the content-addressed design
capsule so new executions do not mutate design identity:

```text
DESIGN-IDENTITY CAPSULE
  canonical authority
  canonical blueprint
  governed C4 structural mappings
  observability-contract authority
  SLI and SLO authority
  applicable SLA authority references
  proof authority
  frozen admission-proof snapshot
  Cross-Apply admission receipt references
  evidence-ledger references

EXECUTION EVIDENCE ESTATE
  test executions
  production executions
  telemetry
  provider testimony
  replay records
```

The capsule can deterministically answer “show me the evidence attributable to
me” by resolving external testimony through its immutable capability, authority,
blueprint, capsule, and execution identities. Only the frozen evidence required
to explain the admission decision may be embedded as an admission-proof
snapshot; general execution history is never capsule content.

### Observability and service-level design

Observability is designed into the circuit before realization. Every executable
cell declares an observability contract alongside its input, energized
responsibility, and result geometry:

```text
EXECUTABLE CELL
  identity and semantic address
  input contract
  event / responsibility / mechanic / native operation
  outcome or result contract

  observability contract
    required testimony checkpoints
    measurement definitions
    correlation and causal identities
    authorized dimensions
    sampling requirements
    evidence destination

  SLI references
  applicable SLO references
  applicable SLA references only at a declared service boundary
```

At scenario altitude, the minimum checkpoints make the semantic lifecycle
attributable: Input admitted or rejected, Event started, responsibility invoked,
provider realization selected and completed when applicable, Outcome admitted
or rejected, and experience closed or left incomplete. Lower-altitude cells use
their own semantic nouns but preserve equivalent attribution to the exact cell,
authority digest, execution identity, provider identity, and parent causal
identity.

Observability authority states what testimony must exist and how it is measured.
Telemetry values are evidence. Available implementation metrics do not become
service indicators merely because a runtime or exporter happens to emit them.

#### SLI, SLO, and SLA remain distinct

An **SLI** defines measured service behavior over admitted testimony. Its
authority binds:

- stable SLI identity and semantic scope;
- the exact testimony identities and admissible dispositions consumed;
- numerator, denominator, aggregation, percentile, or other calculation rule;
- authorized dimensions and grouping rules;
- evaluation window and freshness rule;
- unit; and
- incomplete, missing, duplicate, and late-testimony dispositions.

Semantic indicators such as `experience-closure-rate`, `outcome-admission-rate`,
and `evidence-completeness-rate` are first-class. They preserve the distinction
between physical provider success and semantic Outcome admission.

An **SLO** binds one or more admitted SLI identities to explicit objective
conditions and evaluation windows:

```text
SLI        experience-closure-rate
OBJECTIVE  >= 99.95 percent
WINDOW     rolling 30 days
```

The SLI definition; the SLO objective, window, and error-budget policy; and any
child-budget allocation profile are authority. The observed value, current
compliance disposition, and remaining error budget are runtime evidence.

Root objectives are never inferred by adding child objectives, and child
budgets are never inferred from topology or observed latency. Any decomposition
is explicit authority:

```text
ROOT SLO
  -> governed allocation profile
       child-cell budget A
       child-cell budget B
       reserve / variance budget
```

An **SLA** is an externally governed service commitment. It may bind parties,
service scope, capability or compatibility profile, admitted SLO references,
measurement authority, evaluation period, exclusions, breach dispositions, and
remedy obligations. Every executable cell is observable and may contribute to
SLIs and SLOs; an internal mechanic or provider cell acquires contractual SLA
meaning only when explicit SLA authority binds that declared service boundary.

Admission proves that observability authority is complete, projectable, and
capable of producing attributable testimony. It does not claim that a rolling
production SLO or SLA has been satisfied before its governed evaluation window
has closed over admitted evidence.

#### Observability follows topology

Every executable edge may reference an observability obligation. For a selected
route, the attributable testimony can include the reached junction, selecting
variant, selection authority, elapsed time, input and output digests, execution
identity, branch target, provider identity, and Outcome disposition. The
obligation is blueprint authority; each observed value is evidence.

Fan-out and convergence observability preserves joint necessity. A convergence
view can report each required product's arrival, time-to-ready, join wait, the
last admitted product, and the exact missing-product set. This reveals where the
experience is waiting without replacing the declared convergence requirement
with incidental timing behavior.

### Canonical blueprint geometry

The canonical blueprint is a **typed semantic graph**. ASCII, Mermaid, and the
interactive SideFX surface are deterministic projections of that graph. The
human reviews a map; the machine reasons over the graph; neither reads a picture
someone drew.

The graph therefore expresses **semantic geometry**, not implementation control
flow. A reviewer must be able to see decisionality, joint necessity, readiness,
altitude descent, and semantic advancement without inferring any of them from
generated code, a language-level branch, or the order in which nodes happen to
appear.

#### Fractal cells share geometry without flattening altitude

The scenario cell is the semantic transistor. It carries exactly one Input,
one Event, and one Outcome:

```text
+----------------------------+
| GIVEN / INPUT              |
| admitted-order             |
| contract: order.v1         |
+--------------+-------------+
               |
               v
+----------------------------+
| WHEN / EVENT               |
| qualify-order              |
| responsibility             |
+--------------+-------------+
               |
               v
+----------------------------+
| THEN / OUTCOME             |
| order-qualified            |
| experience established     |
+----------------------------+
```

The scenario cell answers to three governed label lenses. They are translations
of one semantic object, not three structures:

| Lens | Input | Event | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gherkin | GIVEN | WHEN | THEN |
| Circuit | INPUT | EVENT | OUTCOME |
| Experience | DATA | ACTION | EXPERIENCE |

A projection profile declares which scenario lens it renders, and a view may
render more than one. The lens changes labels only. It never changes node
identity, edge semantics, semantic precedence, or digest, and a lens is never a
reason to emit a second blueprint.

Lower altitudes preserve the same three-position geometry without inheriting
Gherkin or experience nouns that do not belong to them:

| Altitude | Cell | First position | Energized position | Result position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Capability | Scenario cell | Input | Event | Outcome / Experience |
| Operation | Execution cell | Input | Responsibility | Result |
| Mechanic | Mechanic cell | Input | Mechanic | Result |
| Provider / physical | Provider cell | Physical Input | Native Operation | Physical Result |

Only scenario altitude owns the promised experience. A hash operation,
filesystem observation, or provider call produces an attributable result; it
does not independently acquire a Gherkin Outcome or redefine the capability's
promise.

#### Typed nodes

Every node carries a declared kind. A projector derives its shape from the kind;
it never chooses a shape to make a diagram read better.

| Node kind | Meaning | ASCII | Mermaid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | Admitted state or product available to a downstream Input | `[ ... ]` | rectangle |
| `responsibility` | Event; the governed thing that must happen | `< ... >` | rectangle |
| `outcome` | Declared result of one responsibility | `[ ... ]` | rectangle |
| `junction` | An Outcome declaring more than one variant | `{ ... }` | rhombus |
| `convergence` | A node whose Input contract requires several upstream products | `[& ... ]` | rectangle with required-product list |
| `provider-slot` | Subordinate governed provider reference | `... PROVIDER` | provider style class |
| `terminal` | Closing experience or disposition | `(( ... ))` | circle |

A junction is not an inserted decision node. It is the declared Outcome itself,
rendered as a junction because canonical authority gave it declared variants.
Projection ordinals make their display deterministic without making one variant
semantically precede another.

#### Typed edges have orthogonal semantics

Arrows are not sequence. Every edge carries exactly one topological role, plus
the contract, progress, and selecting-variant fields applicable to that role.
These dimensions answer different questions and must never be collapsed into
one relation enum:

| Dimension | Closed vocabulary | Declares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Topology | `TRANSITION`, `BRANCH_ROUTE`, `FAN_OUT_MEMBER`, `CONVERGENCE_REQUIREMENT`, `ALTITUDE_DESCENT`, `BOUNDED_RETURN` | What kind of circuit connection this is |
| Contract relation | `SATISFIES`, `REQUIRES` | How a product and an Input contract compose; optional when the edge is not a contract edge |
| Semantic progress | `NARROWS`, `ESTABLISHES`, `TERMINATES`, `DESCENDS`, `BOUNDED_RETURN` | How meaning advances; required for every executable forward transition or governed return |
| Selecting variant | Exact declared Outcome variant | Which variant selected the edge; required for `BRANCH_ROUTE` and for any variant-selected `BOUNDED_RETURN`, otherwise forbidden |

Topology describes circuit geometry. Semantic progress describes advancement.
Contract relations describe compatibility or necessity. The selecting variant
describes decisionality already owned by an Outcome. The vocabularies are
deliberately closed and non-overlapping within each dimension. Extending one is
a governed carrier and projection-profile change, not an authoring convenience.

A branch route is therefore unambiguous:

```text
Outcome A  -- APPROVED / BRANCH_ROUTE / NARROWS -->  Input B
```

A convergence requirement expresses different facts:

```text
Product A  -- CONVERGENCE_REQUIREMENT / REQUIRES -->  Input B
```

An edge is inspectable at its own altitude:

```text
Binding authority   payment-disposition.v1
Topology            BRANCH_ROUTE
Selecting variant   APPROVED
Semantic progress   NARROWS
Target              fulfill-order
```

#### Branch, fan-out, and convergence are different geometry

These three are routinely collapsed into "arrows," and collapsing them destroys
the reviewer's ability to answer the only question that matters at a fork:
**choose one, or close all of them?**

A **branch** makes exactly one path admissible. It originates from an admitted
Outcome variant, never from a language-level condition:

```text
                Payment Disposition {junction}
                  /                    \
 APPROVED / BRANCH_ROUTE / NARROWS   DECLINED / BRANCH_ROUTE / NARROWS
              v                          v
        fulfill-order            resolve-payment-failure
```

A **fan-out** makes several responsibilities independently necessary. All of
them must close:

```text
                  Order Qualified
                        |
              FAN_OUT (all members required)
        +---------------+---------------+
        v               v               v
 Reserve Inventory  Fraud Check    Price Confirm
        |               |               |
        v               v               v
 Stock Reserved    Risk Cleared   Price Confirmed
```

A **convergence** node declares the complete set of upstream products its Input
contract requires before its Event may occur:

```text
[Stock Reserved] -----------------+
                                  |
[Payment Approved] ---------------+--> [Fulfillment Ready]
                                  |
[Risk Cleared] -------------------+

INPUT CONTRACT requires
  stock-reserved
  payment-approved
  risk-cleared
```

Because the required set is declared rather than inferred, readiness is a
computable disposition during execution:

```text
[x] Stock Reserved
[x] Payment Approved
[ ] Risk Cleared

Fulfillment Ready   BLOCKED -- 2/3 required products admitted
```

**Multiple inbound edges are not convergence.** Three alternative branch routes
arriving at one terminal are alternatives; a convergence node requires all of
its declared products jointly. A projector that renders alternative routes as
convergence, or convergence as alternatives, has misstated the circuit and must
fail closed rather than render.

#### Monotonic advancement

Every executable forward transition must narrow admitted state, establish a new
required product, descend to a lower altitude, or terminate an obligation. A
transition that merely moves state sideways has no declarable progress
disposition, and its absence is the point — it should look wrong.

```text
[Raw Order]
    | NARROWS
[Validated Order]
    | NARROWS
[Qualified Order]
    | NARROWS
[Approved Order]
```

Narrowing is also visible over sets, which is often the clearest form of the
proof:

```text
Candidate Set  27
    | NARROWS (filter)
Eligible Set    8
    | NARROWS (select)
Selected        1
```

A back edge is legitimate only when canonical authority declares a bounded
repair, resumption, or iteration and states its bound. An undeclared back edge,
an unexplained widening, and an untyped edge are all holding dispositions, never
warnings a reviewer may pass over.

#### Altitude descent keeps the same geometry

`ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS` is the only forward edge form that changes
altitude. The three-position geometry survives while its semantic nouns become
more physical:

```text
WHY          capability / promised experience
  | ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS
WHAT         scenario circuit
  | ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS
RESPONSIBILITY   execution authority
  | ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS
HOW          operations and mechanics
  | ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS
WHERE        provider slot
  | ALTITUDE_DESCENT / DESCENDS
PHYSICS      native execution
```

Zooming is therefore navigation over declared descent references in one graph.
It is not a set of separately drawn diagrams that must be kept in agreement.

#### Authority and evidence run in opposite directions

The forward direction carries authority; the return direction carries testimony.
The projection must make the two visually and structurally distinct, because
conflating them is exactly how testimony starts to look like admission:

```text
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY / FORWARD     ------------------>
AUTHORITY DESCENT / FORWARD      - - - - - - - - ->
EVIDENCE / RETURN                <. . . . . . . . .
```

Provider binding is forward authority: it permits a responsibility to descend
to a governed provider slot. Provider testimony is evidence returning from
execution. Evidence overlays are always dotted, always return-directed, always
subordinate, and never carry topology, contract, or semantic-progress fields
from the forward edge vocabularies. They bind testimony to canonical node or
edge identities; they are not additional blueprint edges.

#### Canonical legend

Every projection carries the legend for the profile that produced it:

| Element | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[ ... ]` | admitted state or product |
| `< ... >` | event / responsibility |
| `{ ... }` | disposition junction with declared variants |
| `(( ... ))` | terminal experience |
| solid forward arrow | admitted semantic authority flow |
| dashed forward arrow | authority descent or provider binding |
| dotted return arrow | evidence or testimony |
| `variant / TOPOLOGY / PROGRESS` | branch selector, circuit role, and semantic progress for a route |

#### Blueprint views

A view is a governed lens over the one canonical graph. Adding a view adds a
projection profile; it never adds a diagram to maintain:

```text
        CANONICAL BLUEPRINT GRAPH
                    |
      +-------------+-------------+
      v             v             v
    ASCII        Mermaid      SideFX UI
      |             |             |
      +-------------+-------------+
                    |
        same graph, same nodes,
        same edges, same digests
```

Evidence and Runtime / Play views may overlay externally stored testimony on
those identities. Overlay testimony has its own evidence digest and does not
change the canonical graph or blueprint digest.

| View | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Scenario | The full cell circuit with Input / Event / Outcome geometry |
| Monotonic | Semantic advancement only, plus the counted monotonic summary |
| Branch | Junctions, variants, and the routes each variant selects |
| Dependency | Required capabilities, products, and backplane contracts |
| Altitude | Descent references and the cells beneath each responsibility |
| C4 | Context, Container, Component, and optional projected Code mappings from semantic identity to structural realization |
| Provider | Provider slots, modes, and the scenarios bound to them |
| Observability | Required testimony checkpoints, semantic addresses, correlation rules, measurements, dimensions, sampling, and evidence destinations |
| Service Level | SLI definitions, SLO targets and allocations, applicable SLA bindings, and separately digested observed compliance overlays |
| Evidence | Returning testimony against forward semantic addresses |
| Runtime / Play | Live execution state and convergence readiness over the same nodes |
| Semantic diff | Node, edge, relation, variant, and digest delta between two blueprints |

The **Monotonic View** is the visual proof surface. It renders advancement
without implementation detail and states the same fact as counts:

```text
submitted-order
      | TRANSITION / NARROWS
admitted-order
      | TRANSITION / NARROWS
qualified-order
      |
      +-- NOT_QUALIFIED / BRANCH_ROUTE / TERMINATES --> rejected
      |
      +-- QUALIFIED / BRANCH_ROUTE / ESTABLISHES
             |
      +------+------+
      | FAN_OUT_MEMBER (all required)
      v      v      v
 reserved approved cleared
      |      |      |
      +------+------+
             | CONVERGENCE_REQUIREMENT / REQUIRES
    fulfillment-ready
             | TRANSITION / ESTABLISHES
      order-fulfilled

Semantic states                         9
Executable forward transitions         8
  Progress: NARROWS                     2
  Progress: ESTABLISHES                 5
  Progress: TERMINATES                  1
Topology: BRANCH_ROUTE                  2
Topology: TRANSITION                    3
Topology: FAN_OUT_MEMBER                3
Topology: CONVERGENCE_REQUIREMENT       3
Contract relation: REQUIRES             3
Terminal paths                          2
Undeclared back edges                   0
Unexplained state widening              0
Ambiguous transitions                   0

MONOTONIC CIRCUIT      CONFORMS
```

The **Runtime / Play View** is the same graph under actual testimony. It marks
node state, never redefines it:

```text
[x] admit-order            PASS
[x] qualify-order          QUALIFIED
[x] reserve-inventory      PASS
[x] authorize-payment      PASS
[~] fraud-check            RUNNING
[ ] fulfillment-ready      WAITING -- 2/3 required products admitted
[ ] fulfill-order          WAITING
```

Any active edge yields its own testimony against blueprint identities:

```text
Edge topology CONVERGENCE_REQUIREMENT
Contract      payment-approved SATISFIES fulfillment-ready.payment
Authority     sha256:...
Execution     exec:92314
Disposition   SATISFIED
```

The Play view illuminates the route that executed. It remains testimony under
the Evidence Replay Law and does not admit anything.

A **Service-Level View** combines immutable service-level authority with a
separately digested evidence overlay:

```text
CAPABILITY resolve-customer-order
SLA        premium-order-processing.v2

ROOT EXPERIENCE
closure rate      99.96 percent / SLO >= 99.95 percent   CONFORMS
p95 latency       1.82 s        / SLO <= 2.00 s          CONFORMS
error budget      21.4 percent remaining                 EVIDENCE

CIRCUIT
admit-order          42 ms / 100 ms   CONFORMS
qualify-order       118 ms / 150 ms   CONFORMS
reserve-inventory   390 ms / 350 ms   EXCEEDED
authorize-payment   231 ms / 400 ms   CONFORMS
fraud-check         811 ms / 900 ms   CONFORMS
fulfill-order       198 ms / 300 ms   CONFORMS
```

The view must identify the SLI, SLO, allocation, SLA, observation window, and
evidence digests behind every disposition. It cannot calculate a root guarantee
by summing child values or present a partial window as contractual compliance.
Runtime / Play may animate the same overlay as the circuit executes, showing
where service-level budget is consumed without turning the animation into
authority.

### Deterministic canonical blueprint projection

ASCII sketches and Mermaid diagrams are governed presentation profiles over one
canonical blueprint carrier. They are not authored independently and neither is
permitted to become a second blueprint. The same admitted graph authority must
produce both representations. Before final admission, the same rule applies to
one lineage-bound blueprint candidate under review; projection does not make the
candidate canonical or admitted.

The normalized carrier is `canonical-circuit-blueprint.v1`. At minimum it binds:

- capability identity and version;
- source-authority disposition and lineage;
- capability-authority and capsule digests when available;
- canonical-blueprint authority identity and digest;
- semantic precedence as the graph's required partial order;
- deterministic projection ordinals for otherwise independent peer nodes,
  edges, variants, and sets; these ordinals carry no execution meaning;
- every scenario's Input identity and contract;
- every scenario's Event identity and authority;
- every scenario's Outcome identity, contract, and declared variants;
- every node's declared kind — state, responsibility, outcome, junction,
  convergence, provider slot, or terminal experience;
- terminal disposition;
- every edge's topological role, applicable contract relation, applicable
  semantic-progress disposition, selected Outcome variant when branching,
  semantic precedence, projection ordinal, and binding authority;
- for every branch junction, the complete variant-to-target route set;
- for every fan-out, the complete set of jointly required downstream
  responsibilities;
- for every convergence node, the complete set of required upstream products
  that its Input contract demands;
- every declared altitude-descent reference and the cell it descends into;
- any declared back edge together with its bounded repair, resumption, or
  iteration authority;
- subordinate mechanic and provider-slot references;
- governed C4 Context, Container, Component, and optional projected Code
  mappings to structural realization authority;
- every executable cell's observability contract, including required testimony
  checkpoints, semantic and causal addresses, measurements, authorized
  dimensions, sampling requirements, and evidence destination;
- every applicable edge-observability obligation;
- every SLI definition and its exact testimony inputs, scope, calculation,
  dimensions, window, freshness, unit, and missing-testimony disposition;
- every SLO objective, evaluation window, error-budget policy, and governed
  child-budget allocation profile;
- applicable SLA authority references and their declared service boundaries;
- observability Cross-Apply parity requirements; and
- the projection-profile and view authorities permitted for that blueprint.

The carrier must be rejected when required semantic precedence is absent,
ambiguous, cyclic outside a declared bounded return, or inferred only from
object discovery, filesystem order, model output order, or generated
implementation. Independent siblings do not require an arbitrary total semantic
order. Their stable projection ordinals are presentation authority only and
must not become execution precedence. The carrier must also be rejected when a
node carries no declared kind, an edge carries no topological role, an
executable transition carries no progress disposition, a contract edge carries
no contract relation, a branch route or variant-selected bounded return names no
declared Outcome variant, a fan-out set is not jointly required, or a
convergence node does not declare its complete required-product set. It must
also reject an executable cell without sufficient observability authority, an
SLI derived from unspecified or non-admitted testimony, an SLO without an exact
target and evaluation window, an inferred child-budget allocation, an SLA bound
without a declared service boundary, or a Cross-Apply target that cannot
preserve required semantic measurement identity and lineage. A projector must
not invent semantic precedence, insert a decision node, hide a route, straighten
a branch, infer an Outcome variant that canonical authority did not declare, or
supply an edge, observability, structural, or service-level field the carrier
left unstated.

For monotonic circuits, every solid transition advances toward a terminal
Outcome and no back edge reopens earlier meaning. Monotonic does not mean linear:
branching remains visible and every branch is labeled with the exact Outcome
variant that selected it. If canonical authority contains a non-monotonic repair
or resumption edge, the projection must show that back edge rather than making
the circuit appear monotonic.

#### Projection profiles

The first approved presentation profiles are:

| Profile | Required deterministic form |
| --- | --- |
| `sidefx-circuit-blueprint-ascii.v1` | ASCII-only bytes, LF line endings, stable presentation ordinals, explicit Input / Event / Outcome rows, declared node kind, variant-to-target routes carrying topology and progress, junction and convergence markers, authority-descent provider bindings, terminal labels, and the counted monotonic proof block |
| `sidefx-circuit-blueprint-mermaid.v1` | Mermaid `flowchart TD`, stable node identities, one scenario card containing Input / Event / Outcome geometry, kind-derived node shapes, `variant / TOPOLOGY / PROGRESS` edge labels, dashed forward provider bindings, dotted return evidence, and fixed semantic style classes |

The ASCII profile is deliberately restricted to the printable ASCII range so
that it survives every terminal, diff, patch, and log surface without encoding
negotiation. Box-drawing characters are therefore not permitted in
`sidefx-circuit-blueprint-ascii.v1`. A richer box-drawn review lens is a
separate future profile — `sidefx-circuit-blueprint-unicode-box.v1` — and it is
a second projection of the same carrier, never a second blueprint and never a
replacement for the ASCII profile that governed review.

Stable presentation ordinals order independent peers for byte determinism only.
They must be derived from explicit presentation authority or stable semantic
identities with digest-based collision resolution and must never be interpreted
as semantic or runtime precedence.

The Mermaid profile derives node shape from the declared node kind rather than
from reviewer taste: rectangles for scenario and state geometry, rhombus
junctions for Outcomes that declare more than one variant, circles for terminal
experiences, and the provider style class for provider slots. Solid forward
arrows carry semantic authority, dashed forward arrows carry authority descent
and provider bindings, and dotted return arrows carry evidence. Colors remain
light blue for non-terminal scenarios, green for admitted success, orange for
attributable incomplete execution, red for rejection, and violet for provider
slots. Color, shape, and line style are explanatory only: every topology,
contract relation, progress disposition, and variant must also be stated in
text. Outcome
variants own decisionality, so a junction shape marks an Outcome that already
declares variants; the projector must never insert a separate decision node
between a scenario and its declared branches. Where a profile renders one card
per scenario rather than one node per Input, Event, and Outcome, the card takes
the shape of the Outcome it carries — a scenario whose Outcome declares more
than one variant renders as a junction card, and a terminal scenario renders as
a terminal.

The Mermaid profile pins distinct deterministic dash patterns for the two non-
solid channels: long dashes for forward authority descent and short dots for
return evidence. A declared bounded return stays in the solid authority channel
and is distinguished by running against the flow direction, because it carries
governed authority under a declared bound rather than testimony. Direction,
pattern, and text must agree; a label alone cannot repair a line emitted in the
wrong visual channel, and an `ALTITUDE_DESCENT` edge drawn solid is a channel
defect even when its label is correct.

Stable node IDs are derived deterministically from semantic identities, with
digest-based collision resolution. Labels retain the exact semantic identities.
Whitespace, indentation, class order, presentation order, quoting, and final newline are
part of the versioned projection profile. The ASCII and Mermaid source outputs
contain no wall-clock time, machine, user, workspace path, or discovery-order
input.

Mermaid **source determinism** and rendered-image determinism are separate proof
surfaces. Identical blueprint authority, projection capability, and projection
profile must reproduce byte-identical Mermaid source. SVG, PNG, FigJam, or other
physical renders are reproducible only when the Mermaid renderer, layout engine,
configuration, fonts, viewport, and render profile are also version- and
digest-pinned. A renderer upgrade is a physical projection-profile change and
must not silently alter an already reviewed diagram.

#### Replayable projection receipt

Every projection binds a `canonical-circuit-blueprint-projection-receipt.v1`
containing:

- capability identity;
- capability-authority and capsule digests when available;
- canonical-blueprint authority digest;
- projection capability identity and authority digest;
- projection-profile identity and authority digest;
- normalized carrier digest;
- ASCII source digest;
- Mermaid source digest;
- the identity and source digest of every additional view projected from the
  same carrier;
- optional physical-render profile and output digests; and
- `PROJECTED`, `REPLAY_DIVERGED`, or an exact holding disposition.

Replay with the same lineage-bound authority inputs must reproduce the
normalized carrier, ASCII source, Mermaid source, and their digests exactly.
Observation time may be recorded in external testimony, but it is not an input
to the deterministic projection payload.

An Observability or Service-Level **design view** follows that ordinary
projection receipt. A view that overlays observed values additionally carries a
`capability-evidence-overlay-receipt.v1` binding the immutable blueprint and
view digests, evaluation capability and authority digest, exact bounded evidence-
set digest, SLI/SLO/SLA authority digests, evaluation window and cutoff, output
digest, and disposition. The cutoff is evidence-evaluation input, never blueprint
input. Replay over the same authority and bounded evidence set must reproduce
the same observed overlay; a later window produces a new evidence receipt, not a
new capsule or blueprint digest.

#### Human blueprint review

Before capability authority is admitted for collapse, the designated human
reviewer must receive the deterministic ASCII and Mermaid projections, every
required C4, Observability, and Service-Level review view, and their projection
receipt. Human review returns approve, hold, or reject testimony. A
deterministic review-binding capability validates the testimony and emits a
`canonical-blueprint-review-receipt.v1` bound to:

- reviewer authority reference;
- capability-authority digest;
- canonical-blueprint authority digest;
- normalized carrier digest;
- ASCII and Mermaid source digests;
- every required review-view identity and output digest;
- projection-profile digests;
- review disposition; and
- exact findings or reviewer rationale reference.

Human approval does not self-admit the capability. It satisfies the design-review
obligation consumed by deterministic admission alongside contract, identity,
lineage, blueprint-closure, and proof gates. This ADR intentionally makes
designated human blueprint approval a permanent, universal admission obligation,
not a temporary assurance profile. Any mutation to scenario geometry, node
kinds, edge topology, contract relations, progress dispositions, transitions,
variants, fan-out sets, convergence requirement sets, altitude-descent
references, dependencies, mechanics, provider slots, projection profiles,
structural mappings, observability contracts, SLI definitions, SLO objectives
or allocations, applicable SLA bindings, views, or blueprint authority
invalidates the review receipt and requires a new projection and review. A file
described as “human-reviewed” without a current digest-bound receipt is not
evidence of review.

#### Capability ownership

The projection responsibility is substantial and reusable, so it is a dedicated
capability rather than hand-authored formatting inside capsule management:

| Capability | Architectural responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `manage-capability-capsule` | Retains COLLAPSE / REVEAL orchestration, verifies the capsule, selects a declared representation profile, and delegates projection; it does not own ASCII or Mermaid construction |
| `project-capability-revelation` | Composes the public “show me what you are” view set and consumes the blueprint projection bundle; it does not reconstruct topology from a scenario-name list |
| `project-canonical-circuit-blueprint` | New dedicated circuit that resolves `canonical-circuit-blueprint.v1`, projects ASCII, Mermaid, and every declared view from the same carrier with node kinds and orthogonal edge semantics intact, verifies deterministic replay, and binds the projection receipt |
| `prove-canonical-blueprint-geometry` | New dedicated circuit that verifies typed nodes, typed edges, branch variant coverage, jointly required fan-out sets, complete convergence requirement sets, declared back-edge bounds, and monotonic advancement before projection or review |
| `prove-capability-observability-design` | New deterministic circuit that verifies cell and edge observability coverage, semantic attribution, SLI testimony definitions, SLO targets and allocations, SLA boundaries, and Cross-Apply parity before review |
| `evaluate-capability-service-level` | New deterministic circuit that evaluates admitted SLI/SLO/SLA authority over a bounded external evidence set and emits attributable compliance and error-budget testimony without modifying design identity |
| `bind-canonical-blueprint-review` | New dedicated circuit that binds human approve / hold / reject testimony to exact blueprint and projection digests and emits the review receipt |
| Capability-authority admission circuit | Requires a current approved review receipt and proves that its digests still match the candidate authority before admission eligibility |
| Mermaid render provider | Optional subordinate physical renderer for SVG, PNG, FigJam, or another visual target; never the source of blueprint meaning |

The new projection circuit has this root geometry:

```text
CAPABILITY project-canonical-circuit-blueprint
  I canonical-circuit-blueprint-projection-request.v1
  E project-canonical-circuit-blueprint.v1
  O canonical-circuit-blueprint-projection-bundle.v1

  SCENARIOS
    resolve-canonical-circuit-blueprint
    project-canonical-circuit-blueprint-ascii
    project-canonical-circuit-blueprint-mermaid
    project-declared-blueprint-lenses
    verify-canonical-circuit-blueprint-replay
    bind-canonical-circuit-blueprint-projection-receipt
```

The new review-binding circuit has this root geometry:

```text
CAPABILITY bind-canonical-blueprint-review
  I canonical-blueprint-review-request.v1
  E bind-canonical-blueprint-review.v1
  O canonical-blueprint-review-receipt.v1

  SCENARIOS
    admit-blueprint-review-boundary
    obtain-human-blueprint-review-testimony
    bind-blueprint-review-disposition
    verify-blueprint-review-digest-closure
```

Human review is the only nondeterministic effect in the second circuit. The
reviewer supplies testimony through a governed human-provider slot; deterministic
authority admits the review request, binds the exact decision, and verifies
digest closure. Neither the person nor the provider self-admits the capability.

The call relationship is:

```text
manage-capability-capsule / REVEAL
  -> project-capability-revelation
     -> project-canonical-circuit-blueprint
        -> ASCII source + Mermaid source + projection receipt

candidate capability authority
  -> project-canonical-circuit-blueprint
  -> bind-canonical-blueprint-review
  -> capability-authority admission circuit
  -> manage-capability-capsule / COLLAPSE
```

The existing `project-capability-revelation` capability declares an execution
circuit view, but its current carrier contains only scenario identity and name,
and its current Mermaid projection is a generic `Input -> scenario list` shape.
That view cannot express transitions, Outcome variants, Input / Event / Outcome
geometry, terminal dispositions, or provider slots. It is superseded by the
dedicated blueprint projection circuit above and must become its consumer.

`manage-capability-capsule` may expose `ascii`, `mermaid`, or a combined
`blueprint-review` revelation profile, but adding those profiles does not move
projection meaning into the manager. The manager delegates to the admitted
projector and returns its receipt unchanged.

### Blueprint-guided high-fidelity authoring

The canonical blueprint is both the capability's design identity and the
fabrication map for its authoring conveyor. It is not a diagram added after a
model has authored companion authority. The design phase produces and admits a
lineage-bound blueprint before the fabrication phase asks a model to fill any
scenario-authority gap. Every later authoring request, inspection, integration,
closure decision, human view, and proof obligation must resolve from that same
blueprint digest.

Blueprint authority carries design decisions. Model testimony may help propose
a blueprint candidate during the design phase, but it does not make the
candidate canonical. Deterministic conformance, deterministic projection,
digest-bound human review, and blueprint admission establish the fixed map.
During fabrication, a governed author model proposes declarative meaning only
inside one selected blueprint cell. It cannot select the cell or revise the map.

This separates two governed circuits:

| Circuit | Governing question | Model role | Admission boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blueprint design | What exact capability circuit should exist? | May propose a lineage-bound blueprint candidate from the canonical feature and admitted precedents | Deterministic blueprint conformance plus digest-bound human review |
| Blueprint-guided fabrication | What declarative authority closes this one designed cell? | May propose one bounded scenario or altitude fragment | Deterministic fragment admission, integration, and whole-blueprint closure |
